To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The study of 10 cases of vaginal drainage of amniotic fluid after premature rupture of membranes revealed that fetal pulmonary maturity could be predicted by the lecithin/sphingomyelin ratio.

the use of a single amniotic fluid phospholipid index (PI) value of less than 2.0 in the presence of a positive L/S ratio and a positive TDx-FLM value for the diagnosis of fetal pulmonary maturity is associated with a high false-positive rate.

we have shown that amniotic fluid can be collected from the vagina after rupture of membranes in a patient treated with antenatal corticosteroids, that the biochemical analysis of this fluid can be used for the prediction of fetal lung maturity and that it is necessary to perform appropriate biochemical tests for the detection of urine contamination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an efficient method for predicting the outcome of premature rupture of the fetal membranes.
the development of an efficient and robust method to predict the onset of the first symptoms of the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of dexamethasome to induce fetal lung maturity in patients with premature rupture of membranes is not indicated.
the use of amniotic fluid in the management of preterm labour is not recommended.
there is a significant association between maternal serum and amniotic fluid alpha-fetoprotein concentrations and fetal growth retardation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of amniotic fluid for the assessment of fetal lung maturity should be restricted to patients with intact membranes, whereas in patients with ruptured membranes, amniotic fluid can be used for the assessment of lung maturity only when the liquor has been aspirated from the vagina and has been shown to be free of maternal urine.
the amniotic fluid from the vagina is a good sample for assessing fetal pulmonary maturity.

, in the absence of any clinical evidence of infection and if the amniotic fluid is not contaminated with maternal urine, the biochemical tests for fetal pulmonary maturity may be performed on liquor draining vaginally.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the L/S ratio and/or the PtdIns ratio in amniotic fluid from women with premature rupture of the membrane is not reliable for predicting fetal maturity.
the amniotic fluid is an important source of fetal lung fluid.

, in the case of a patient with premature rupture of the membrane, vaginal discharge of liquor should not be discarded as it may be useful in determining fetal lung maturity and thus help in deciding the mode of delivery and management.
